title: Wire protocols
description: The wire shapes a model server speaks (F2 B5), as data: how to build a request, where to read the answer, how an error answer maps to a failover trigger. A shape is a row; adding one needs no code change. Templates: {model}, {key} and {prompt} are replaced inside any string, a string that is exactly {max_tokens} becomes the integer. The host is never in this file; a connection supplies it. Pointers are RFC 6901. The mock provider (bin/mock_provider.py) serves any shape from this file.

id.description: A neutral name of the API style.

path.description: Path template; holds {model} or the body does.

headers.description: Header templates; the key placeholder {key} goes here and nowhere else.

body.description: Body template: messages, tools, max tokens.

output_shape.description: How the link enforces output shape: {enforcement id: body pointer where the schema or grammar goes} (used by the mock).

logprobs.description: Pointer to the list of per-token items ({token, logprob}) an answer carries when the link exposes log probabilities (used by the mock).

usage_keys.description: Names of the input and output token counts inside usage (used by the mock to build an answer).

usage_extra.description: Optional (F2c B): where an answer shows the cache-write, cache-read and reasoning token counts, each as a pointer inside the usage object. included_in names the count the provider already adds them to (input or output: bin/cost.py takes them out so the five counts are disjoint), or null when it counts them apart. A shape that shows none of them has no usage_extra.

tool_calls_sample.description: The value found at the tool_calls pointer in an answer with a tool call; the string {arguments} is the tool arguments (used by the mock).

errors.description: First match wins: put the more specific rows (a body pattern) first.

body_pattern.description: A regex searched in the raw body.

sample_body.description: A body the server sends for this error (used by the mock); it matches body_pattern.

models_list.description: How the model list answer is laid out (used by the mock): the list at pointer items, each model as an object whose field holds prefix + the model id.

family.description: Item field that holds the model family (used by the mock).

version.description: Item field that holds the model version (used by the mock).

pointer.description: RFC 6901 pointer inside the usage object.
